html:
The Guarijío are a Uto-Aztecan people of the Sierra Madre Occidental on the border of Sonora and Chihuahua in northwest Mexico, along the upper Mayo River. Their language is close to that of the Rarámuri, or Tarahumara.

They farm maize, beans and squash on mountain slopes and hunt and gather in the canyons. Jesuit missionaries reached them in the 1600s, and they took part in revolts against the missions. In the 1900s ranchers took much of their land, and in the 1970s and 1980s the Sonoran Guarijío campaigned for it and won back part of it. They number a few thousand. Their neighbours include the Mayo to the west.
